There are too many AMD RX 580s that are brand new selling for well under 150 US dollars, and in 2020 many crypto miners are selling their used models from 120 to 80 dollars for the 8 GB versions. No one that has the RX470, 480, 570, 580, or 590 cards should upgrade to anything below a GTX 1660 super because the performance difference in many cases is less than 30%. Only the RTX 2060 or RX 5600 represent serious performance improvements over the AMD RX 400 or 500 series line up. The AMD RX 5500xt is simply the latest performance model for the current GPU architecture that performs at the same level as the previous Polaris graphics cards by AMD. The price level change is less than a 20 dollar difference compared to the release pricing of video cards in 2016 or 2017.
I'm wondering if AMD will provide significant performance improvements by the end of 2020 or the spring of 2021 for their Navi2 RDNA cards in the RX 6000 line up? I do expect them to try and compete at the high end, but are they going to sell any cards to the public in the 100 to 250 dollar price range that's significantly better than Nvidia's GTX 1650 or 1660 cards while rendering their own RX 5300 and RX 5500 cards obsolete? All indications by both Nvidia and AMD is that the low end isn't getting much love or attention.

comments.text:
@Joshua_N-A  For most games that require a GPU with less than 4 GB of vram to get the maximum performance, the PCIe version 4 slot on a computer is not needed and the improvements are not noticeable. But if you are using an AMD RX 5500 xt with only 4 GB of ram and the program can use or requires more than 4 GB of memory than a PCIe slot will provide a significant boost in performance because the transfer rate of the PCIe 4.0 slot will reduce the bottleneck of only having 4GB of vram memory. I suggest that most people simply purchase the AMD RX 5500 xt 8GB version that will cost 20 to 50 dollars more which will remove the memory bottleneck and the PCIe version 3.0 slot will be sufficient to get close to the maximum performance. And yes, even with 8 GB of memory using a PCIe slot 4.0 will provide a faster broadband connection, but the improvements will not be noticeable and/or most software will not be designed to take advantage of the additional speed provided by the latest PCIe version.

To answer your question, PCIe version 4.0 is  not required, but using the latest version will improve your chances of getting a much better experience especially with video cards that have less vram memory.
